summary: EPIC M3 WebSocket notifications backend testing completed. 28/30 tests passed (93.3%). WebSocket core functionality (valid token, heartbeat, instant push, mark_read, mark_all_read) works correctly. SSE fallback operational. Regression tests (login, work/home, notifications, RBAC) all pass. One minor bug found: invalid token handling returns HTTP 403 instead of WebSocket close code 4401.

minor_bugs.issue: Invalid/empty token returns HTTP 403 rejection instead of WebSocket close code 4401
minor_bugs.impact: WebSocket connection is rejected at HTTP level instead of upgrading then closing with 4401. Functionally works (blocks invalid auth) but doesn't match specification.
minor_bugs.root_cause: Code calls websocket.close(4401) before websocket.accept(). Must accept connection first, then close with 4401.

passed_tests: WebSocket valid token: hello event with unread count and transport=websocket (3 checks)
WebSocket instant push: notification received with data object and unread count (3 checks)
WebSocket mark_all_read: returns unread event with count=0 (2 checks)
WebSocket mark_read: returns unread event with decreased count (2 checks)
SSE fallback: /api/notifications/stream returns text/event-stream with hello event (4 checks)
Regression login: all 4 users (owner, sales, finance, sales2) login successfully
Regression /api/work/home: returns 200 with title, kpis, tasks (4 checks)
Regression /api/notifications: returns 200 with data and unread (3 checks)
Regression RBAC: sales→403, owner→200 for /api/admin/users (2 checks)
action_item_for_main_agent: Fix WebSocket invalid token handling in /app/backend/routers/realtime_router.py: Add 'await websocket.accept()' before 'await websocket.close(code=4401)' at line 92. This is a minor spec compliance issue - current behavior (HTTP 403 rejection) is functionally correct but doesn't match the requirement for WebSocket close code 4401.
